title: Treasury Sanctions Cambodian Senator Kok An and Scam Center Network Defrauding Americans
summary: OFAC designated Cambodian Senator Kok An and 28 individuals/entities in his network for operating scam compounds that have stolen millions from U.S. victims through digital asset investment fraud. This action is part of the Scam Center Strike Force effort coordinated with DOJ, FBI, and USSS, and includes the seizure of 503 fraudulent web domains. Americans lost at least $10 billion in 2024 to Southeast Asia-based scam operations, a 66 percent increase over the prior year.
key_points: OFAC designated Kok An (Cambodian senator) and 28 associated individuals/entities for operating scam compounds that defraud Americans via digital asset investment fraud
Seizure of 503 fraudulent web domains and a social media messaging app used to recruit victims
U.S. Secret Service previously took action against U.S.-based individuals who laundered over $73 million from this network in 2024
Americans lost at least $10 billion to Southeast Asia-based scams in 2024, up 66% from prior year
Action aligned with Executive Order 14390 (March 6, 2026) Combating Cybercrime, Fraud, and Predatory Schemes
State Department offering rewards of up to $10 million for information on Tai Chang scam compound proceeds and up to $4 million for arrest of fugitive Daren Li
why_it_matters: This is a Treasury sanctions action targeting overseas fraud networks involved in digital asset investment scams. While it removes some fraudulent platforms from the ecosystem, it does not constitute a macro catalyst or market structure event. It falls under financial stability/crime enforcement rather than monetary policy or market operations.
important_numbers: $10 billion (American losses to Southeast Asia scams in 2024)
$10 million (State Dept reward for Tai Chang info)
